chunks: The man whom I appointed as the governor of Egypt,
was a man who was sincere to us, and severe and hostile towards our enemies.
May Allah have mercy on him!
He has indeed completed his days and met his death, while we were pleased with him.
May Allah grant him His pleasure, and multiply the reward for him.
ai.seo_question: What qualities did Imam Ali look for in his governors according to this letter?
ai.summary: In this letter to Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) uses Malik al-Ashtar as the ideal model of governance, highlighting the dual virtues of internal sincerity (nasihah) and external firmness against adversaries. This passage underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of righteous leadership and the divine approval of those who serve the community with integrity, framing political authority as a trust that yields spiritual reward.
